title: Tall parents have shorter children, on average: regression
body: Galton noticed children of very tall parents tend to be tall but closer to average, and symmetrically for short parents. No force pulls families toward mediocrity; extremes are partly luck, and luck does not inherit. Regression to the mean thereafter explained phantom effects of punishments, remedies and coaching interventions everywhere.
source_hint: Galton, 'Regression Towards Mediocrity in Hereditary Stature' (1886)
